purpose: Engine-level smoke coverage for the The Broken Script 2.0 Bedrock port.

content_log.capture: Enable Content Log File and Content Log GUI before opening the world; preserve the latest log for the run.

bindings.candidate_commit: exact full 40-hex Git SHA for the checkout under test
bindings.artifact_sha256: exact full 64-hex SHA-256 of the packaged .mcaddon

scenarios.title: Fresh-world creation and pack initialization
preconditions: Create a new world from the fixed seed and exact runtime contract.
Attach the generated .mcaddon and enable the Beta APIs experiment.
steps: Open the world and wait 30 seconds after the first player spawn.
Run `/scriptevent tbs:help` and `/scriptevent tbs:events` as the operator.
Confirm the custom pack is listed in world settings and keep the content log open.
pass_criteria: The world opens without a pack-load dialog or script initialization error.
The help response appears and the event count is returned.
The content log contains no pack-loading error or parity-critical warning.

scenarios.title: World and player save, quit, and reload
preconditions: Complete the bootstrap scenario in the same world.
Use one named test player and leave at least one known inventory slot available.
steps: Run `/scriptevent tbs:adv can_you_see_me` and record the title/message.
Run `/scriptevent tbs:arena start`, note the arena state, then save and quit to the title screen.
Reopen the same world, run the advancement and arena commands again, and then stop the arena.
pass_criteria: The already-awarded advancement is not awarded a second time after reload.
World initialization does not reset the saved arena or progression state unexpectedly.
No dynamic-property serialization or migration error appears in the content log.

scenarios.title: Death and respawn with active story, quest, boss, and effect state
preconditions: Use a copy of the persistence world after its first successful reload.
Keep cheats enabled and have the operator at the fixed overworld spawn.
steps: Award `can_someone_hear_me`, apply both developer effects, and start the arena state.
Summon `thebrokenscript:integrity_phase_1` and record the player and boss state before death.
Run `/kill @s`, respawn, wait 30 seconds, and inspect the content log and arena cleanup.
pass_criteria: The player respawns without a script exception and player state remains scoped to that player.
Boss and arena state either follows the documented cleanup path or remains active without duplicate controllers.
Temporary effects and entity references do not produce stale-handle errors after respawn.

scenarios.title: Leave, rejoin, and server-restart persistence
preconditions: Use a world with a known player advancement and a known world-state marker.
For the server-restart leg, use Bedrock Dedicated Server or the platform's equivalent full process restart.
steps: Leave the world with the player state active and record the content-log timestamp.
Rejoin, verify the player state and world state, then stop the server process cleanly.
Start the server again, rejoin with the same player, and repeat the state checks.
pass_criteria: Player leave/rejoin does not duplicate subscriptions or reset per-player dynamic properties.
A clean server restart preserves world state and reloads the pack once.
No duplicate-event, stale-entity, or initialization errors are introduced by either reconnect.

scenarios.title: Two-player and multi-player ownership and targeting
preconditions: Use two distinct player accounts on the same world; add a third player when a server is available.
Place players at least 32 blocks apart before starting the encounter.
steps: Award a different advancement to each player and apply an effect to only player A.
Start the arena and summon one boss near player A while player B remains outside the participant radius.
Move player B into the radius, reconnect player A, and observe targeting, damage attribution, and cleanup.
pass_criteria: Player-scoped state, effects, advancement flags, and coordinates do not leak between players.
Boss participant and target selection remains stable when a player joins, leaves, or re-enters.
Damage, projectile ownership, and cleanup do not cross-attribute to the wrong player.

scenarios.title: Dimension travel, return, safe arrival, and failure recovery
preconditions: Use a fresh world after bootstrap and keep the player at the fixed overworld spawn.
Test both a custom realm and a vanilla return destination.
steps: Run `/scriptevent tbs:dim clan_void` and wait for the readiness-gated teleport to complete.
Verify the landing platform, dimension id, player state, and return route, then run `/scriptevent tbs:dim overworld`.
Repeat once with the destination region unloaded or an invalid dimension id and record the failure response.
pass_criteria: Custom-dimension registration and first-entry initialization complete without a script error.
The player arrives on safe footing, returns to the intended dimension, and retains player state.
Invalid or unavailable destinations fail visibly and do not strand or corrupt the player.

scenarios.title: Boss start, abort, death, reconnect, victory, cleanup, and replay prevention
preconditions: Use a disposable copy of the smoke world with cheats enabled.
Have one-player and two-player runs available; do not reuse an encounter after a failed cleanup.
steps: Start the arena, summon Integrity phase 1, and record encounter participants and active sounds/effects.
Run separate abort, player-death, and player-reconnect attempts; then complete a victory attempt using the supported test setup.
After each attempt, wait for cleanup, inspect entities and state, and try to start the encounter a second time.
pass_criteria: Every terminal path converges to the documented cleanup state with no duplicate arena generation.
Participant tracking, audio, projectiles, effects, and entity references are cleared or retained exactly as documented.
Replay prevention works after victory and a new encounter can start only when the source rules permit it.

scenarios.title: Story thresholds and one-shot progression
preconditions: Use a fresh world with one online player for the complete threshold run.
Record the exact story-clock tick at the beginning and after every threshold.
steps: Run the story clock continuously through days 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 24, 32, 38, and 48 while the player remains online.
Record every title, action bar, book, coordinate, moon, and progression side effect at the threshold where it occurs.
Save, reload, and pass each crossed threshold again; verify one-shot events remain consumed and no earlier threshold fires twice.
pass_criteria: Every registered threshold fires at its documented tick and in source order.
One-shot story events remain consumed across reload and do not duplicate after reconnect.
The content log contains no threshold handler exception or failed persistence write.

scenarios.title: Event suppression during boss arenas and other suppressors
preconditions: Use a fresh world with the ambient event system initialized.
Have the content log capture enabled at Info or Verbose level.
steps: Observe the world for the configured ambient-event window and record normal event output.
Start an arena and repeat the same observation window while suppression is active.
Stop or abort the arena, wait for cleanup, and observe one final window for correct resumption.
pass_criteria: Normal ambient events can run before the suppressor is active.
Suppressed event families do not fire while the boss arena or documented suppressor is active.
Events resume once and only once after cleanup, with no leaked timers or duplicate subscriptions.

scenarios.title: Runtime diagnostics and release-blocking classification
preconditions: Enable Content Log File and Content Log GUI before beginning any scenario.
Preserve the complete log and annotate each message with the scenario and timestamp that produced it.
steps: Review the content log after every scenario, including pack load, reload, reconnect, dimension, boss, and story transitions.
Classify each error or warning as parity-critical or non-critical using the report schema; do not discard warnings silently.
Run the report validator locally and, for a release candidate, with `--require-complete`.
pass_criteria: The report contains a diagnostic entry or an explicit empty diagnostics list for every completed run.
Any parity-critical error or warning makes the report validator fail.
A release-tag workflow cannot pass without a complete, validated runtime report.
